questions.question: Bad braking technique:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Bad braking technique causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: When riding, wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to help other drivers see you. Reflective clothing works even better.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Only watch what is in front of you.
Only watch what is behind you.
Watch what is happening in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is ahead of you, but also what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked regularly by riders.
Do not exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes. Make it part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that indicate bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see if drivers behind you are paying attention and slowing down. This helps you know if they see you stopping.

questions.question: The best clothing for riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You like, regardless of other vehicles.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best and where you have space around your motorcycle. Good riders change position as conditions change.

questions.question: To handle a tailgater safely:

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass if you can do so safely. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a green arrow before turning.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles sold in the United States after 1978 turn the headlight on automatically when running. Always check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: When scanning the area around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Whether you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: When looking for hazards, focus on escape routes in or near intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware. What does the "S" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use it to make decisions while riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, what should you look for?

options.text: A loose fit that flaps in the wind.
A snug fit that does not flap in the wind.
A jacket not made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: A snug fit that does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or other sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap, but loosely enough to allow free movement.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose and flapping in the wind.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you while staying comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands while riding. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: No matter what helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet works best when it meets safety standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle ride is to:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long rides, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and reduces your risk of a collision. Always watch the other drivers around you so you can predict their moves.
